learningObjectives: Explain the physiological or methodological basis of Multiple Comparisons.
Apply Multiple Comparisons to technically valid clinical interpretation.
Identify artifacts, confounds and limits that could alter conclusions.
Communicate findings without exceeding the evidence or professional scope.

mechanismMap.label: Core concept
mechanismMap.detail: QEEG may test many electrodes, bands and metrics simultaneously, increasing chance findings.

mechanismMap.label: Mechanism
mechanismMap.detail: Correction procedures, preregistered hypotheses and replication reduce false discovery. Clinical reports should distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analyses.

mechanismMap.label: Clinical integration
mechanismMap.detail: Protects clinicians and clients from impressive but unreliable maps.

mechanismMap.label: Boundary condition
mechanismMap.detail: Cherry-picking the most extreme map after seeing all results is circular reasoning.

quizBank.question: Which statement best captures Multiple Comparisons?
options: QEEG may test many electrodes, bands and metrics simultaneously, increasing chance findings.
It provides a stand-alone psychiatric diagnosis
It is unaffected by state and artifact
Its interpretation requires no clinical context
quizBank.explanation: QEEG may test many electrodes, bands and metrics simultaneously, increasing chance findings.

quizBank.question: What is the safest clinical principle for Multiple Comparisons?
options: Integrate raw signal quality, state, method and clinical context
Assume a coloured map shows exact anatomy
Treat statistical rarity as proof of disorder
quizBank.explanation: EEG and QEEG interpretation requires converging evidence, technical validity and clinical context.

quizBank.question: Which error is most important to avoid in Multiple Comparisons?
options: Cherry-picking the most extreme map after seeing all results is circular reasoning.
quizBank.explanation: Cherry-picking the most extreme map after seeing all results is circular reasoning.

reviewPrompts.answer: Correction procedures, preregistered hypotheses and replication reduce false discovery. Clinical reports should distinguish exploratory from confirmatory analyses.
Protects clinicians and clients from impressive but unreliable maps.
Cherry-picking the most extreme map after seeing all results is circular reasoning.
The more you look, the stricter your evidence must become.
